columns.autofillPrompt: The legal name of the other party to this contract, i.e. the party that is not {{OUR_COMPANY}}. Use the name exactly as written in the parties block.

Classify the document from {{OUR_COMPANY}}'s point of view: Customer agreement if {{OUR_COMPANY}} provides goods or services to the other party; Supplier agreement if {{OUR_COMPANY}} buys from them; Partner agreement for distribution, reseller or alliance deals; License, Lease, Financing or Data processing when that is the main subject; Amendment if the document amends an earlier agreement; otherwise Other.
The effective date of this agreement (or of this amendment). Return only the date.
The date the current term ends. If the contract states a term length instead of an end date, compute the end date from the effective date. Leave empty if the agreement has no fixed end.
Yes if the term renews automatically unless a party gives notice; No if it simply expires or renews only by mutual agreement; Unclear otherwise.
The number of days of advance written notice required to prevent renewal or to terminate at the end of the term. Convert months to days (1 month = 30 days). Empty if none.
The governing law jurisdiction, e.g. 'Washington, USA'.
The total or annual contract value in US dollars if stated; empty if not stated.

rows.Title: Payments we owe
rows.Description: Fees, rent, interest, support fees, repayments or milestone payments we must pay, with amount and due date or schedule. Merge late charges into the same item.
rows.Examples: Licensee shall pay the annual fee on or before the first day of each contract year. | Borrower shall repay all advances on the maturity date.

rows.Title: Payments owed to us
rows.Description: The counterparty's payment terms on our invoices. Party Counterparty, so receivables can be chased.
rows.Examples: Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after receipt.

rows.Title: Rebates, fund contributions, true-ups and deposit top-ups
rows.Description: Calculated payments tied to a period or event: volume rebates, marketing fund contributions, true-up invoices, restoring a security deposit.
rows.Examples: Within 45 days after each quarter, pay the rebate earned for that quarter with a calculation statement.

rows.Title: Supplier price-increase limits and notice
rows.Description: The other side may raise what we pay only within a cap and after notice. Counterparty, Event-driven.
rows.Examples: Provider may increase fees once per year by up to 5% on 60 days' prior written notice.

rows.Title: Periodic operational report
rows.Description: Recurring service-level, sales, inventory or usage reports due after each period.
rows.Examples: Within 20 days after each calendar quarter, deliver a report of net sales and inventory on hand.

rows.Title: Financial statements and compliance certificates
rows.Description: Lender or investor reporting: periodic financial statements and officer-signed compliance certificates.
rows.Examples: Within 45 days after each fiscal quarter, deliver a compliance certificate signed by the CFO.

rows.Title: Non-renewal notice before automatic renewal
rows.Description: Last day to stop an auto-renewing contract or service. Due date = term end minus the notice period.
rows.Examples: Either party may give notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.

rows.Title: Renewal, extension or transition option window
rows.Description: A right that lapses unless exercised by a deadline or inside a window (renewal or extension option, transition assistance request). Due date = last day; note when the window opens.
rows.Examples: Tenant may exercise the option by notice no earlier than 12 and no later than 9 months before expiration.

rows.Title: Renewal decision before fixed expiry
rows.Description: A contract that ends on a date without automatic renewal: decide and sign any renewal before expiry. Created when expiry is within 12 months.
rows.Examples: This agreement expires on its stated date and may be renewed only by a written agreement signed before then.

rows.Title: Termination for convenience notice
rows.Description: Notice either party must give to end the contract without cause. Event-driven.
rows.Examples: Either party may terminate this agreement for convenience on 60 days' prior written notice.

rows.Title: Fee-increase notice we must give
rows.Description: Our price increase at renewal is valid only if notice is given by a deadline.
rows.Examples: Supplier may increase fees for a renewal term by giving notice at least 60 days before that term starts.

rows.Title: Change-of-control or assignment notice
rows.Description: Notice due after a change of control, merger or assignment. Event-driven.
rows.Examples: Distributor shall notify Supplier in writing within 30 days after any change of control.

rows.Title: Audit cooperation
rows.Description: The other side's audit right creates our duty to cooperate after their notice. Our own discretionary audit rights are not tracked.
rows.Examples: On 30 days' notice, Customer may audit Supplier's records once per year; Supplier shall cooperate.

rows.Title: License usage certification or true-up
rows.Description: Periodic certification of users, seats or volumes, and payment for any excess.
rows.Examples: Within 30 days after each anniversary, certify the peak number of named users.

rows.Title: Compliance deliverables: certificates, attestations and plans
rows.Description: Reports, certificates or plans due on a date or each year: SOC reports, inspection or permit certificates, continuity or security plans. The other side's delivery is Counterparty.
rows.Examples: Processor shall deliver an updated SOC 2 Type II report by October 1 each year. | Within 60 days, deliver an updated disaster recovery plan.

rows.Title: Restrictive covenants and pricing commitments
rows.Description: Standing restrictions to monitor: exclusivity, non-compete, license-use limits, most-favoured pricing and the duty to extend better pricing.
rows.Examples: Licensee shall not permit any affiliate or third party to use the software.

rows.Title: Financial covenants and default notices
rows.Description: Minimum liquidity or ratio covenants, and notifying a lender or counterparty of a default within a set time.
rows.Examples: Borrower shall notify the bank within five business days after becoming aware of any default.

rows.Title: Service-level commitment
rows.Description: Measurable service levels (availability %, response or resolution times), ours or the other side's. Ongoing.
rows.Examples: Provider shall maintain monthly availability of at least 99.9%.

rows.Title: Service credits: issue or claim within the window
rows.Description: Credits we must issue after a miss, or credits we must claim before the window closes.
rows.Examples: To receive a service credit, Customer must submit a claim within 30 days after the end of the month.

rows.Title: Maintain insurance and deliver certificates
rows.Description: Keep required coverage and deliver certificates or endorsements by a date or each year. One item, dated by the certificate.
rows.Examples: Maintain general liability insurance and deliver a certificate of insurance by January 15 each year.

rows.Title: Confidentiality
rows.Description: Protect the other side's confidential information during the term and any survival period. Usually Both, Ongoing.
rows.Examples: Each party shall hold the other party's confidential information in confidence.

rows.Title: Personal data breach notification
rows.Description: Notify of a personal data or security breach within a set time. Event-driven.
rows.Examples: Processor shall notify Controller of any personal data breach within 48 hours after becoming aware of it.

rows.Title: Sub-processor notice and objection window
rows.Description: The processor's advance notice of new sub-processors, and our window to object.
rows.Examples: Controller may object in writing within 15 days after receiving notice of a new sub-processor.

rows.Title: Minimum purchase or volume commitment
rows.Description: Minimum spend or volume per period; a shortfall triggers a remedy.
rows.Examples: Distributor shall purchase products of at least $500,000 in each contract year.

rows.Title: Forecasts and periodic commercial reviews
rows.Description: Rolling forecasts and scheduled pricing or business reviews.
rows.Examples: By the 5th of each month, provide a rolling six-month forecast.

rows.Title: Product discontinuation and last-time-buy notice
rows.Description: The supplier's notice before discontinuing a product. Counterparty, Event-driven.
rows.Examples: Supplier shall give at least 90 days' notice before discontinuing any product.

rows.Title: Defect, damage or repair notice window
rows.Description: Notice we must give within a set time after delivery or discovery, or rights are lost.
rows.Examples: Buyer shall notify Supplier of any defect within 14 days after delivery.

rows.Title: Post-signing deliverable
rows.Description: A one-time commercial plan or setup task due within a set time after the effective date.
rows.Examples: Within 90 days after the effective date, submit an initial marketing plan for approval.

rows.Title: Key personnel continuity
rows.Description: Named key people who may not be replaced without notice or approval.
rows.Examples: Supplier shall not replace the named account director without Customer's prior written approval.

rows.Title: Contacts, notice addresses and invoicing logistics
rows.Description: Designating contacts, notice addresses, where invoices go, issuing our own routine invoices. Payment amounts and deadlines are tracked separately.
rows.Examples: Each party shall designate a point of contact. | Invoices shall be sent to the accounts payable mailbox.

rows.Title: Good-faith cooperation and general conduct
rows.Description: General promises to cooperate or act in good faith, with no action, date or deliverable.
rows.Examples: The parties shall cooperate in good faith in the performance of this agreement.

rows.Title: Interpretive and legal boilerplate
rows.Description: Headings, counterparts, own costs, governing law, entire agreement, severability, force majeure, survival, waivers, liability caps, termination for cause, remedies.
rows.Examples: Headings are for convenience only. | Each party shall bear its own costs.

rows.Title: Routine service delivery and site rules
rows.Description: Uniforms, badges, site access, hours, permitted use, signage, service descriptions and general performance standards with no measurable level, trigger, date or deliverable.
rows.Examples: Supplier staff shall wear uniforms and identification badges. | Provider will perform the services in a professional manner.

rows.Title: Conditions met at signing
rows.Description: Payments, deposits or deliverables completed at or before signing, including conditions to effectiveness of an agreement now in effect.
rows.Examples: As a condition to effectiveness, Borrower shall pay the facility fee on the closing date.

rows.Title: Efforts-based or third-party duties
rows.Description: Reasonable or best efforts duties with no measurable outcome, and duties placed on affiliates, subcontractors or others who did not sign.
rows.Examples: Reseller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to promote the products.

rows.Title: Indemnity claim notices and defense procedures
rows.Description: Procedural duties after a third-party claim (prompt notice, defense, cooperation); Legal decides case by case.
rows.Examples: The indemnified party shall promptly notify the indemnifying party of any claim.

rows.Title: Record retention and end-of-term data return
rows.Description: Keep records for a period, or return or delete data at the end of the contract; often defined in another document.
rows.Examples: Upon termination, Processor shall return or delete all personal data within 30 days.

theme.name: Obligation Hub
theme.basedOn: Atmospheric Precision: graphite #111827 text, ice blue #9AC7F5 and cloud #EAF3FC accents, violet #8B83DB tertiary, white background
theme.note: Applied with the ThemeManager REST API by the deploy script (site owner). There is no SharePoint IQ tool for it; on the Cowork path pick a theme by hand or run the deploy script with pagesOnly: true.

manual: Navigation: Settings (gear) > Change the look > Navigation: Site navigation visible, horizontal; then Edit on the site navigation and add the links in the order of site.navigation.nodes.
Header: Settings > Change the look > Header: Layout Compact, Background (emphasis) None.
Logo: Settings > Change the look > Header > Site logo > Change, and upload deploy/assets/obligation-hub-logo.png.

Theme: Settings > Change the look > Theme. A custom theme palette can only be applied by script (deploy-obligation-hub.js with pagesOnly: true, or a tenant admin adding it as a company theme); otherwise pick the closest built-in blue theme.

workflows.name: Capture new contracts
workflows.triggerText: When a file is added to the Contracts library
workflows.prompt: Create an AI workflow named "Capture new contracts" on this site. Trigger it when a file is added to the Contracts library. For each run, load the site skill capture-obligations from AgentAssets/Skills and follow it for the file that triggered the run. Save results without asking for confirmation. Run as me.

workflows.name: Capture changed contracts
workflows.triggerText: When a file in the Contracts library is changed
workflows.prompt: Create an AI workflow named "Capture changed contracts" on this site. Trigger it when a file in the Contracts library is changed. For each run, load the site skill capture-obligations from AgentAssets/Skills and follow it for the file that triggered the run. If the contract text is unchanged since the last capture, log the skip and stop. Save results without asking for confirmation. Run as me.

workflows.name: Assign owners

For each run, load the site skill obligation-owner-digest from AgentAssets/Skills and follow it for the Obligations list. It may send each owner one email or Teams message. Run as me.

For each run, load the site skill obligation-leadership-digest from AgentAssets/Skills and follow it. It may send one email to the leadership recipients in AgentAssets/Config/hub-settings.json and post to their Teams channel. Run as me.

autofill.note: Autofill may not run on every tenant; capture reads the contract text itself and never depends on it.
autofill.copilotPrompt:
Turn on autofill for the Contracts library on this site. Use these existing columns and extraction prompts, keep values that are already filled in (don't overwrite), and don't create new columns:
- Counterparty: The legal name of the other party to this contract, i.e. the party that is not {{OUR_COMPANY}}. Use the name exactly as written in the parties block.
- ContractType: Classify the document from {{OUR_COMPANY}}'s point of view: Customer agreement if {{OUR_COMPANY}} provides goods or services to the other party; Supplier agreement if {{OUR_COMPANY}} buys from them; Partner agreement for distribution, reseller or alliance deals; License, Lease, Financing or Data processing when that is the main subject; Amendment if the document amends an earlier agreement; otherwise Other.
- EffectiveDate: The effective date of this agreement (or of this amendment). Return only the date.
- ExpirationDate: The date the current term ends. If the contract states a term length instead of an end date, compute the end date from the effective date. Leave empty if the agreement has no fixed end.
- AutoRenews: Yes if the term renews automatically unless a party gives notice; No if it simply expires or renews only by mutual agreement; Unclear otherwise.
- NoticePeriodDays: The number of days of advance written notice required to prevent renewal or to terminate at the end of the term. Convert months to days (1 month = 30 days). Empty if none.
- GoverningLaw: The governing law jurisdiction, e.g. 'Washington, USA'.
- ContractValue: The total or annual contract value in US dollars if stated; empty if not stated.
- ContractSummary: Two plain-language sentences, under 250 characters in total: what the contract is for and the most important dates or commitments.
